sanskrit: svargaṃ manujaśārdūla gaccheyaṃ sahitā tvayā apatyāya ca māṃ gaccha tvam eva kurunandana
english: I would go to heaven together with you, O tiger among men; come to me for the sake of offspring, O joy of the Kurus.

sanskrit: na hy ahaṃ manasāpy anyaṃ gaccheyaṃ tvad ṛte naram tvattaḥ prativiśiṣṭaś ca ko 'nyo 'sti bhuvi mānavaḥ
english: For I would not approach any other man even in thought apart from you; and who else is there in the world more excellent than you?

sanskrit: imāṃ ca tāvad dharmyāṃ tvaṃ paurāṇīṃ śṛṇu me kathām pariśrutāṃ viśālākṣa kīrtayiṣyāmi yām aham
english: Now hear this ancient story rooted in dharma from me, O wide-eyed one, which I shall recount — a tale widely celebrated.

sanskrit: vyuṣitāśva iti khyāto babhūva kila pārthivaḥ purā paramadharmiṣṭhaḥ pūror vaṃśavivardhanaḥ
english: There was of old a king known as Vyushitashva, supremely devoted to righteousness, the extender of the lineage of Puru.

sanskrit: tasmiṃś ca yajamāne vai dharmātmani mahātmani upāgamaṃs tato devāḥ sendrāḥ saha maharṣibhiḥ
english: When that righteous and great-souled one was performing sacrifice, the gods together with Indra and the great sages came thither.

sanskrit: amādyad indraḥ somena dakṣiṇābhir dvijātayaḥ vyuṣitāśvasya rājarṣes tato yajñe mahātmanaḥ
english: Indra became exhilarated with soma, and the twice-born with the sacrificial fees, at the great sacrifice of that royal sage Vyushitashva.

sanskrit: vyuṣitāśvas tato rājann ati martyān vyarocata sarvabhūtāny ati yathā tapanaḥ śiśirātyaye
english: Then Vyushitashva, O king, shone beyond all mortals, surpassing all creatures as the sun surpasses them at the end of winter.

sanskrit: sa vijitya gṛhītvā ca nṛpatīn rājasattamaḥ prācyān udīcyān madhyāṃś ca dakṣiṇātyān akālayat
english: That best of kings, conquering and subduing the monarchs of the east, north, and the middle regions, brought the southern kings to submission.

sanskrit: aśvamedhe mahāyajñe vyuṣitāśvaḥ pratāpavān babhūva sa hi rājendro daśanāgabalānvitaḥ
english: At the great horse sacrifice, the valorous Vyushitashva, that lord of kings, was possessed of the strength of ten elephants.

sanskrit: apy atra gāthāṃ gāyanti ye purāṇavido janāḥ vyuṣitāśvaḥ samudrāntāṃ vijityemāṃ vasuṃdharām apālayat sarvavarṇān pitā putrān ivaurasān
english: Even now those who know the ancient lore sing this verse about him: Vyushitashva, having conquered this earth up to the shores of the sea, protected all the social orders as a father protects his own sons.

sanskrit: yajamāno mahāyajñair brāhmaṇebhyo dadau dhanam anantaratnāny ādāya ājahāra mahākratūn suṣāva ca bahūn somān somasaṃsthās tatāna ca
english: Performing great sacrifices, he gave wealth to the brahmins; having collected unlimited riches, he conducted great rites, pressed many soma-libations, and spread out soma ceremonies.

sanskrit: āsīt kākṣīvatī cāsya bhāryā paramasaṃmatā bhadrā nāma manuṣyendra rūpeṇāsadṛśī bhuvi
english: He had a wife most highly esteemed, Kakshivati's daughter, named Bhadra, O lord of men, unrivalled in beauty on earth.

sanskrit: kāmayām āsatus tau tu parasparam iti śrutiḥ sa tasyāṃ kāmasaṃmatto yakṣmāṇaṃ samapadyata
english: They two loved each other passionately — so the tradition says; overcome with desire for her, he contracted consumption.

sanskrit: tenācireṇa kālena jagāmāstam ivāṃśumān tasmin prete manuṣyendre bhāryāsya bhṛśaduḥkhitā
english: Before long he set like the sun, and when that lord of men was dead, his wife was overwhelmed with grief.

sanskrit: aputrā puruṣavyāghra vilalāpeti naḥ śrutam bhadrā paramaduḥkhārtā tan nibodha narādhipa
english: Childless, the deeply afflicted Bhadra lamented piteously — so we have heard; know this, O lord of men.

sanskrit: nārī paramadharmajña sarvā putravinākṛtā patiṃ vinā jīvati yā na sā jīvati duḥkhitā
english: O best knower of dharma, every woman deprived of a son who lives without her husband does not truly live — she lives in misery.

sanskrit: patiṃ vinā mṛtaṃ śreyo nāryāḥ kṣatriyapuṃgava tvadgatiṃ gantum icchāmi prasīdasva nayasva mām
english: For a woman, death without her husband is better, O bull among Kshatriyas; I wish to follow your path — be gracious and take me with you.

sanskrit: tvayā hīnā kṣaṇam api nāhaṃ jīvitum utsahe prasādaṃ kuru me rājann itas tūrṇaṃ nayasva mām
english: Bereft of you I cannot bear to live even a moment; show grace to me, O king, take me swiftly from here.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhato 'nugamiṣyāmi sameṣu viṣameṣu ca tvām ahaṃ naraśārdūla gacchantam anivartinam
english: I shall follow behind you, O tiger among men, as you go on without turning back, through level and uneven paths alike.

sanskrit: chāyevānapagā rājan satataṃ vaśavartinī bhaviṣyāmi naravyāghra nityaṃ priyahite ratā
english: Like a shadow that does not depart, O king, ever devoted to your will, I shall be, O tiger among men, always intent on your welfare and delight.

sanskrit: adya prabhṛti māṃ rājan kaṣṭā hṛdayaśoṣaṇāḥ ādhayo 'bhibhaviṣyanti tvad ṛte puṣkarekṣaṇa
english: From this day forward, O king, terrible mental agonies that wither the heart will overwhelm me without you, O lotus-eyed one.

sanskrit: abhāgyayā mayā nūnaṃ viyuktāḥ sahacāriṇaḥ saṃyogā viprayuktā vā pūrvadeheṣu pārthiva
english: Surely in my misfortune, O king, unions with companions were severed in previous lives, or associations were broken.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ karmabhiḥ pāpaiḥ pūrvadeheṣu saṃcitam duḥkhaṃ mām anusaṃprāptaṃ rājaṃs tvadviprayogajam
english: And this sorrow born of separation from you has caught up with me now, O king — accumulated in former bodies by sinful deeds.

sanskrit: adya prabhṛty ahaṃ rājan kuśaprastaraśāyinī bhaviṣyāmy asukhāviṣṭā tvaddarśanaparāyaṇā
english: From this day forward, O king, I shall lie on a bed of kusha grass, filled with wretchedness, my whole aim set only upon seeing you again.

sanskrit: darśayasva naravyāghra sādhu mām asukhānvitām dīnām anāthāṃ kṛpaṇāṃ vilapantīṃ nareśvara
english: Show yourself to me, O tiger among men — to me who is wretched, helpless, miserable, and lamenting; be gracious, O lord of men.

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ tasyāṃ vilapantyāṃ punaḥ punaḥ taṃ śavaṃ saṃpariṣvajya vāk kilāntarhitābravīt
english: While she thus lamented in many ways again and again and clasped that corpse, a disembodied voice is said to have spoken.

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha bhadre gaccha tvaṃ dadānīha varaṃ tava janayiṣyāmy apatyāni tvayy ahaṃ cāruhāsini
english: Rise, Bhadra; go — I will grant you a boon here; I shall beget offspring upon you, O fair-smiling one.

sanskrit: ātmīye ca varārohe śayanīye caturdaśīm aṣṭamīṃ vā ṛtusnātā saṃviśethā mayā saha
english: On my own bed, O fair-limbed one, on the fourteenth or the eighth night after your purifying bath at the appointed season, lie down with me.

sanskrit: evam uktā tu sā devī tathā cakre pativratā yathoktam eva tad vākyaṃ bhadrā putrārthinī tadā
english: Thus addressed, that goddess devoted to her husband did exactly as was said; Bhadra, desiring sons, did exactly as instructed.

sanskrit: sā tena suṣuve devī śavena manujādhipa trīñ śālvāṃś caturo madrān sutān bharatasattama
english: That goddess bore sons by him — the corpse — O lord of men: three Shalvas and four sons of Madra, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tathā tvam api mayy eva manasā bharatarṣabha śakto janayituṃ putrāṃs tapoyogabalānvayāt
english: In the same way you too, O bull of the Bharatas, are able by the power of austerity and spiritual discipline to beget sons in me by mental resolve alone.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tayā rājā tāṃ devīṃ punar abravīt dharmavid dharmasaṃyuktam idaṃ vacanam uttamam
english: Vaishampayana said: Thus addressed by her, the king, that knower of dharma, spoke again to that goddess this most excellent speech in accordance with righteousness.

sanskrit: evam etat purā kunti vyuṣitāśvaś cakāra ha yathā tvayoktaṃ kalyāṇi sa hy āsīd amaropamaḥ
english: Exactly so did Vyushitashva act in former times, O Kunti, as you have described, O auspicious one — for he was like an immortal.

sanskrit: atha tv imaṃ pravakṣyāmi dharmaṃ tv etaṃ nibodha me purāṇam ṛṣibhir dṛṣṭaṃ dharmavidbhir mahātmabhiḥ
english: But now I shall speak of this dharma — hear it from me: the ancient usage seen by the great-souled knowers of dharma among the seers.

sanskrit: anāvṛtāḥ kila purā striya āsan varānane kāmacāravihāriṇyaḥ svatantrāś cārulocane
english: Women were unrestrained in former times, O fair-faced one, roaming freely as they pleased, independent, O lovely-eyed one.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ vyuccaramāṇānāṃ kaumārāt subhage patīn nādharmo 'bhūd varārohe sa hi dharmaḥ purābhavat
english: When they went to other men from girlhood, apart from their husbands, O blessed one, there was no unrighteousness, O fair-limbed one — for that was the law in ancient times.

sanskrit: taṃ caiva dharmaṃ paurāṇaṃ tiryagyonigatāḥ prajāḥ adyāpy anuvidhīyante kāmadveṣavivarjitāḥ purāṇadṛṣṭo dharmo 'yaṃ pūjyate ca maharṣibhiḥ
english: Even today creatures born in animal wombs follow that ancient law, free from desire and aversion; this dharma as seen by the ancients is still honored by the great seers.

sanskrit: uttareṣu ca rambhoru kuruṣv adyāpi vartate strīṇām anugrahakaraḥ sa hi dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Among the Northern Kurus even today that eternal dharma prevails, O Rambhoru, which confers freedom on women.

sanskrit: asmiṃs tu loke nacirān maryādeyaṃ śucismite sthāpitā yena yasmāc ca tan me vistarataḥ śṛṇu
english: But in this world not long ago this boundary-rule was established, O pure-smiled one — hear from me at length by whom and for what reason.

sanskrit: babhūvoddālako nāma maharṣir iti naḥ śrutam śvetaketur iti khyātaḥ putras tasyābhavan muniḥ
english: There was a great seer named Uddalaka — so we have heard; his son, the sage who became known as Shvetaketu.

sanskrit: maryādeyaṃ kṛtā tena mānuṣeṣv iti naḥ śrutam kopāt kamalapatrākṣi yadarthaṃ tan nibodha me
english: This boundary-rule was established by him among humans — so we have heard — out of anger, O lotus-eyed one; hear from me the reason for it.

sanskrit: śvetaketoḥ kila purā samakṣaṃ mātaraṃ pituḥ jagrāha brāhmaṇaḥ pāṇau gacchāva iti cābravīt
english: Before Shvetaketu's very eyes, a brahmin took his mother by the hand in his father's presence and said, "Let us go."

sanskrit: ṛṣiputras tataḥ kopaṃ cakārāmarṣitas tadā mātaraṃ tāṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā nīyamānāṃ balād iva
english: The son of the seer then became angry and indignant when he saw his mother being led away thus as if by force.

sanskrit: kruddhaṃ taṃ tu pitā dṛṣṭvā śvetaketum uvāca ha mā tāta kopaṃ kārṣīs tvam eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ
english: Seeing him enraged, his father said to Shvetaketu: "Do not be angry, my son — this is the eternal law."

sanskrit: anāvṛtā hi sarveṣāṃ varṇānām aṅganā bhuvi yathā gāvaḥ sthitās tāta sve sve varṇe tathā prajāḥ
english: "For the women of all social orders are unrestrained on earth, my son; just as cattle are, so are people, each within their own social order."

sanskrit: ṛṣiputro 'tha taṃ dharmaṃ śvetaketur na cakṣame cakāra caiva maryādām imāṃ strīpuṃsayor bhuvi
english: But the seer's son Shvetaketu could not accept that law, and he established this boundary-rule for men and women on earth.

sanskrit: mānuṣeṣu mahābhāge na tv evānyeṣu jantuṣu tadā prabhṛti maryādā sthiteyam iti naḥ śrutam
english: Among humans, O greatly blessed one, but not among other creatures — from that time this rule has been established, so we have heard.

sanskrit: vyuccarantyāḥ patiṃ nāryā adya prabhṛti pātakam bhrūṇahatyākṛtaṃ pāpaṃ bhaviṣyaty asukhāvaham
english: From this day forward, for a woman who goes to another man abandoning her husband, the sin shall be equal to the slaying of an embryo — a painful transgression.

sanskrit: bhāryāṃ tathā vyuccarataḥ kaumārīṃ brahmacāriṇīm pativratām etad eva bhavitā pātakaṃ bhuvi
english: Likewise for a man who violates a woman who was chaste from girlhood and devoted to her husband, this same sin will apply on earth.

sanskrit: patyā niyuktā yā caiva patny apatyārtham eva ca na kariṣyati tasyāś ca bhaviṣyaty etad eva hi
english: And for the wife who is directed by her husband for the purpose of offspring yet refuses to comply, this same sin will befall her as well.

sanskrit: iti tena purā bhīru maryādā sthāpitā balāt uddālakasya putreṇa dharmyā vai śvetaketunā
english: Thus in ancient times this righteous boundary-rule was forcibly established, O timid one, by Shvetaketu, the son of Uddalaka.

sanskrit: saudāsena ca rambhoru niyuktāpatyajanmani madayantī jagāmarṣiṃ vasiṣṭham iti naḥ śrutam
english: And Madayanti, O Rambhoru, appointed for the production of offspring, went to the seer Vasishtha by Saudasa's direction — so we have heard.

sanskrit: tasmāl lebhe ca sā putram aśmakaṃ nāma bhāminī bhāryā kalmāṣapādasya bhartuḥ priyacikīrṣayā
english: From this she received a son named Ashmaka, that beautiful woman, the wife of Kalmashapada, desiring to please her husband.

sanskrit: asmākam api te janma viditaṃ kamalekṣaṇe kṛṣṇadvaipāyanād bhīru kurūṇāṃ vaṃśavṛddhaye
english: Our own birth is also known to you, O lotus-eyed one — that we were born of Krishna Dvaipayana for the flourishing of the Kuru lineage, O timid one.

sanskrit: ata etāni sarvāṇi kāraṇāni samīkṣya vai mamaitad vacanaṃ dharmyaṃ kartum arhasy anindite
english: Considering all these reasons, you ought to carry out this righteous request of mine, O blameless one.

sanskrit: ṛtāv ṛtau rājaputri striyā bhartā yatavrate nātivartavya ity evaṃ dharmaṃ dharmavido viduḥ
english: "A husband should not be disobeyed by his wife in each fertile season, O princess devoted to your vow" — thus those who know dharma know this law.

sanskrit: śeṣeṣv anyeṣu kāleṣu svātantryaṃ strī kilārhati dharmam etaṃ janāḥ santaḥ purāṇaṃ paricakṣate
english: In all other remaining times, a woman indeed is entitled to independence — good people describe this as the ancient dharma.

sanskrit: bhartā bhāryāṃ rājaputri dharmyaṃ vādharmyam eva vā yad brūyāt tat tathā kāryam iti dharmavido viduḥ
english: Whatever a husband commands his wife, O princess, whether righteous or even unrighteous, that must be carried out accordingly — so those who know dharma declare.

sanskrit: viśeṣataḥ putragṛddhī hīnaḥ prajananāt svayam yathāham anavadyāṅgi putradarśanalālasaḥ
english: Especially one who is eager for sons yet is himself lacking in the power of procreation — as I am, O blameless-limbed one, longing to behold a son.

sanskrit: tathā raktāṅgulitalaḥ padmapatranibhaḥ śubhe prasādārthaṃ mayā te 'yaṃ śirasy abhyudyato 'ñjaliḥ
english: With palms reddened and resembling lotus petals, O auspicious one, this folded salutation is raised by me to your head to beg your grace.

sanskrit: manniyogāt sukeśānte dvijātes tapasādhikāt putrān guṇasamāyuktān utpādayitum arhasi tvatkṛte 'haṃ pṛthuśroṇi gaccheyaṃ putriṇāṃ gatim
english: By my direction, O beautiful-haired one, from a twice-born man excelling in austerity, you ought to beget sons endowed with virtues; for your sake, O broad-hipped one, I would reach the path of those who have sons.

sanskrit: evam uktā tataḥ kuntī pāṇḍuṃ parapuraṃjayam pratyuvāca varārohā bhartuḥ priyahite ratā
english: Thus addressed, Kunti then replied to Pandu, the conqueror of enemy cities — that fair-limbed woman devoted to her husband's welfare and delight.

sanskrit: pitṛveśmany ahaṃ bālā niyuktātithipūjane ugraṃ paryacaraṃ tatra brāhmaṇaṃ saṃśitavratam
english: "As a young girl in my father's house, appointed to the honor of guests, I attended there upon a fierce brahmin of sharp-edged vow."

sanskrit: nigūḍhaniścayaṃ dharme yaṃ taṃ durvāsasaṃ viduḥ tam ahaṃ saṃśitātmānaṃ sarvayatnair atoṣayam
english: "He whose resolve in dharma is hidden — him they know as Durvasa; him I gratified with every effort, that one of disciplined soul."

sanskrit: sa me 'bhicārasaṃyuktam ācaṣṭa bhagavān varam mantragrāmaṃ ca me prādād abravīc caiva mām idam
english: "That blessed one declared to me a boon connected with invocation; he gave me a group of mantras and also spoke this to me."

sanskrit: yaṃ yaṃ devaṃ tvam etena mantreṇāvāhayiṣyasi akāmo vā sakāmo vā sa te vaśam upaiṣyati
english: "Whichever god you summon with this mantra, whether reluctantly or willingly, he will come under your control."

sanskrit: ity uktāhaṃ tadā tena pitṛveśmani bhārata brāhmaṇena vacas tathyaṃ tasya kālo 'yam āgataḥ
english: "So I was told at that time in my father's house by that brahmin, O Bharata — that true word of his; now the time for it has come."

sanskrit: anujñātā tvayā devam āhvayeyam ahaṃ nṛpa tena mantreṇa rājarṣe yathā syān nau prajā vibho
english: "With your permission, O king, I shall summon a god, O royal sage, with that mantra, so that we may have progeny, O lord."

sanskrit: āvāhayāmi kaṃ devaṃ brūhi tattvavidāṃ vara tvatto 'nujñāpratīkṣāṃ māṃ viddhy asmin karmaṇi sthitām
english: "Tell me which god I shall summon, O best of knowers of truth; know me as standing ready in this matter, awaiting your permission."

sanskrit: pāṇḍur uvāca adyaiva tvaṃ varārohe prayatasva yathāvidhi dharmam āvāhaya śubhe sa hi deveṣu puṇyabhāk
english: Pandu said: This very day, O fair-limbed one, prepare yourself duly and summon Dharma, O auspicious one — for he is the meritorious one among the gods.

sanskrit: adharmeṇa na no dharmaḥ saṃyujyeta kathaṃ cana lokaś cāyaṃ varārohe dharmo 'yam iti maṃsyate
english: "Our son born of dharma will in no way be tainted by unrighteousness, O fair-limbed one; and this world will regard this as righteous."

sanskrit: dhārmikaś ca kurūṇāṃ sa bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ dattasyāpi ca dharmeṇa nādharme raṃsyate manaḥ
english: "He will be righteous and the Kurus' heir — there is no doubt; even though begotten through delegation, his mind will not delight in unrighteousness."

sanskrit: tasmād dharmaṃ puraskṛtya niyatā tvaṃ śucismite upacārābhicārābhyāṃ dharmam ārādhayasva vai
english: "Therefore, placing dharma foremost, restrained and pure-smiled, worship Dharma with ritual service and invocation."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sā tathoktā tathety uktvā tena bhartrā varāṅganā abhivādyābhyanujñātā pradakṣiṇam avartata
english: Vaishampayana said: Thus directed by her husband, that beautiful woman assented saying "So be it"; saluting him and receiving his leave, she circumambulated him.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca saṃvatsarāhite garbhe gāndhāryā janamejaya āhvayām āsa vai kuntī garbhārthaṃ dharmam acyutam
english: Vaishampayana said: When a year had passed since Gandhari's pregnancy, O Janamejaya, Kunti summoned the infallible Dharma for the sake of a child.

sanskrit: sā baliṃ tvaritā devī dharmāyopajahāra ha jajāpa japyaṃ vidhivad dattaṃ durvāsasā purā
english: That goddess hastened and offered oblations to Dharma; she muttered the mantra given long ago by Durvasa, according to prescribed rite.

sanskrit: saṃgamya sā tu dharmeṇa yogamūrtidhareṇa vai lebhe putraṃ varārohā sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ varam
english: Uniting with Dharma who bore the form of yogic power, that fair-limbed woman obtained a son — the foremost among all living beings.

sanskrit: aindre candrasamāyukte muhūrte 'bhijite 'ṣṭame divā madhyagate sūrye tithau puṇye 'bhipūjite
english: In the auspicious lunar mansion presided over by Indra, in the eighth muhurta called Abhijit, when the sun was at midday, on a holy and honored lunar day —

sanskrit: samṛddhayaśasaṃ kuntī suṣāva samaye sutam jātamātre sute tasmin vāg uvācāśarīriṇī
english: — Kunti at the proper time brought forth a son of abundant glory; and the moment that son was born, a disembodied voice spoke.

sanskrit: eṣa dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭho bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ yudhiṣṭhira iti khyātaḥ pāṇḍoḥ prathamajaḥ sutaḥ
english: "This one will be the foremost among upholders of dharma — there is no doubt; known as Yudhishthira, the first-born son of Pandu."
